sections.h2: Which Carteret County office handles property tax?
sections.html:
Assessing and collecting both run through one Tax Administration office under an appointed Tax Administrator. The commissioners make the appointment. Office staff also serve the review board that hears value appeals.

Walk-in service is on the first floor of the Administration Building, 302 Courthouse Square in Beaufort, and at a Western Office at 701 Cedar Point Blvd., Cedar Point, NC 28584. The phone is 252-728-8485. Hours at both are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays, holidays excepted.

The office handles appraisal, assessment, billing and collection on real, business and personal property. Before listing, ask it what is owed on your parcel and whether a relief claim is on file.

September 1 is the due date. Interest waits until January 6 of the following year. It starts at 2% for January and adds 0.75% each month after.

Key dates and rules

Carteret's fiscal year 2026-27 rate is 22.5 cents for every $100 of assessed value. Real and personal property get separate bills. Property in Beaufort, Bogue, Cape Carteret, Cedar Point, Emerald Isle, Morehead City or Peletier gets one bill with county and town tax combined. Mailed checks are credited by postmark.

sections.h2: How to appeal your assessed value
sections.html:
Send the Real Property Appeal Form to the Tax Administration Office within the window on your value notice. A reappraisal notice gives you 30 days from the date it carries. The appeal covers assessed value alone; the rate and the bill itself are off the table.

The last general reappraisal used a January 1, 2025 market value. Compare your property's characteristics and nearby sales against what the county used. The assessor is presumed to have acted in good faith, so the burden is yours. Useful evidence includes sales of similar nearby homes, damage photos and repair quotes.

  • First level: the Board of Equalization and Review, nine local residents counting two alternates, which mails its Notice of Decision within a month of meeting.
  • Second level: the state Property Tax Commission, where you file within 30 days after the notice arrives. Hearings are typically in Raleigh, and a lawyer may be needed.
  • Third level: the North Carolina Court of Appeals, only on a question of law, and then the state Supreme Court.

Boats, aircraft, mobile homes and business equipment take a different path. Your clock is 30 days from the annual bill's date. The county then sets a conference and rules afterward. The result can go down, up or stay put, and it applies only from that year onward. G.S. 105-290 sets the 30-day window to reach the Property Tax Commission.

North Carolina offers three ways to cut a home's bill, and an owner can take only one. Apply at the county tax office.

  • Age or disability: for homeowners who are 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, and earn no more than $38,800 for 2026. The reduction is $25,000 or one half of value, whichever is greater.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 of appraised value is excluded for a qualifying disabled veteran or an unmarried surviving spouse, and age and income do not matter.
  • Circuit breaker: the cap on the bill is 4.0% of income, rising to 5.0% for incomes above $38,800 and up to $58,200. Qualifying takes five years of owning and living in the house. Tax above the cap is deferred rather than erased.

The application is Form AV-9. File it during the January listing period if you can, because the assessor must accept it until June 1. Renew a circuit breaker claim every year. If you sell, die or move out, three years of deferred tax come due. The rules sit in G.S. 105-277.1, 105-277.1B and 105-277.1C.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Carteret County tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay online, by phone, by mail or in person. The portal accepts cards, eCheck and PayPal. The line at 1-888-544-9433 takes card payments if you have the bill in hand.

  • Mail: a check payable to County of Carteret, sent to PO Box 96264, Charlotte, NC 28296-6264.
  • Counter: at the Beaufort or Cedar Point office, with cash, check, money order or card.
  • Drop box: at the courthouse entrance, no cash, processed the next business day.

Card fees apply: a $1.50 flat charge for an eCheck and 2.50% plus $0.30 a transaction on credit cards. Partial payments in any amount are allowed online, but the full balance must be in before delinquency, and the phone line does not take partial amounts. If a full payment is out of reach, a hardship payment arrangement is available by application. Interest keeps running under it, but it may lower the odds of garnishment or foreclosure.

sections.h2: What happens when taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The lien stays on the parcel, interest keeps growing, and the county can use enforcement tools. G.S. 105-355 attaches the lien to the parcel from the listing date, along with any penalties, interest and costs.

Tools include wage and bank garnishment, state income tax refund setoff, setoff against lottery winnings, attachment of rent, seizure and sale of personal property, and foreclosure on real property. Foreclosure under G.S. 105-374 resembles a mortgage foreclosure and ends at an auction on the courthouse steps, followed by a commissioner's report and a ten-day window for higher bids. Until the sale is confirmed, the owner can still redeem by paying everything owed.

A sale ahead of that is usually the cleaner exit. Once a delinquent account is advertised, the foreclosure process moves forward. If you are behind, call 252-728-8485 before the March 1 to June 30 publication period.

sections.h2: Selling a Carteret County home with taxes owed
sections.html:
A tax balance follows the parcel as a lien, so it is normally cleared at closing. Get a current payoff number from the Tax Administration Office. Then work out with the closing attorney how this year's bill is split.

Recording the deed is its own errand at the register of deeds, described on the Carteret County register of deeds page. A circuit breaker deferral on the property comes due on a transfer, covering the three prior years.

A practical order for a sale: phone 252-728-8485 or stop at the Beaufort counter, ask for the balance on each bill tied to the parcel, and learn whether the town added its share to a combined bill. Then tell your closing attorney about any appeal still open or any relief claim on file, because those change the number. In a cash sale the buyer skips a lender's escrow setup, so the tax figure is simply paid out of your proceeds on the closing date. Keep the receipts and the closing statement with your records.

The county had 70,469 residents on July 1, 2025, in 54,293 housing units. The 2020-2024 median for an owned home is $333,300, with owners living in 74.7% of units.

faqs.q: What is the Carteret County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The 2026-27 county rate is 22.5 cents per $100. Parcels inside a town add the town rate and arrive on one combined bill.

faqs.q: When do Carteret County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On January 6, after the September 1 due date. Pay by January 5 and no interest is owed. After that, 2% applies for January and 0.75% for each month beyond.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Carteret County assessment?
faqs.a: Thirty days, counted from the value change notice for real property and from the bill date for personal property. Only value can be challenged.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Carteret County tax bill in person?
faqs.a: Walk in at Beaufort or at the Western Office in Cedar Point. Both keep weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. A drop box at the courthouse entrance accepts checks.

faqs.q: Can Carteret County set up a payment plan?
faqs.a: Yes, in limited cases. The county offers a hardship payment arrangement by application and lets owners pay in partial amounts before delinquency. Interest still accrues under a plan.
